# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (best overall clip-on), about $199**
- Runner's World and WIRED both like them for clear sound, comfort, and physical buttons that are easy to use mid-run.
- Downsides are IPX4 water resistance and about 7 hours per charge. Runner's World also says Bose has a new pair coming soon, so you may want to wait.
- Price: $199 (down from $299). [Runner's World review](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) | [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (best bone conduction), $125 to $180**
- They leave your ears fully open. Battery is 12 hours, they're rated IP55, and they have physical buttons. WIRED calls them the best for runners who want more bass but still want awareness.
- Downsides are that the neckband can interfere with long hair and winter hats, and clarity is a bit below the older OpenRun.
- Price: $180 list, with $125 listed at REI and Best Buy. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/) | [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Shokz OpenDots 2 (best for long runs and bad weather), $200**
- WIRED's top pick overall. Battery is 10 hours (40 with the case) and the IP57 rating handles rain. They're clip-ons that leave the top of your ear free for glasses or a hat. [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Nothing Ear (Open) (SoundGuys' pick for running), about $99**
- Strong bass for an open design, a good app EQ, and an IP54 rating. SoundGuys lists it at $99 on Amazon (MSRP $149). [SoundGuys open-ear guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) | [SoundGuys workout guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)

**Soundcore AeroFit 2 (best budget hook style), about $80 to $104**
- It has an ear hook, IP55 rating, and 10 hours per charge (42 with the case). SoundGuys lists it at $79.99 on Amazon. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- Dealectric, a deal-tracking site, shows the Soundcore store price as $129.99 and $104 with code AFSC20 (tested 2026-10-22). That is higher than the Amazon price above, so compare before using the code. [Buy at Soundcore via Dealectric (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2) | [Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2)

**Cheapest way to try clip-ons: JLab Flex Open (about $40) or Soundpeats PearlClip Pro (about $50)**
- Both have less bass and detail than the premium pairs, but they're a low-risk way to see if you like the style. Runner's World lists the JLab at $40 in one place and $50 in its text, so check the price at checkout. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) | [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Quick guide**
- Maximum awareness: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2
- Best sound: Bose Ultra Open
- Rain and long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2
- Value: Nothing Ear (Open) or AeroFit 2

Open-ear designs don't guarantee safety, so keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.

The search results gave me review pages rather than direct product listings. The retailer links (Amazon, Best Buy, REI, Walmart) are on the review pages above, and prices change often.
